tool_executions.arguments:
{"prompt":"In the Twin file manager repo (Go, Bubble Tea; see CLAUDE.md for conventions), `readDirectory` in fs.go skips an entry whose `entry.Info()` fails and only calls `log.Printf` (fs.go, inside the `for _, entry := range entries` loop). That error never reaches the user: it is not passed to `m.reportError`, and `log.Printf` writes to stderr while Bubble Tea owns the alt screen, which can corrupt the display. Phase 0's goal is "Twin never fails silently".

Fix it so these per-entry failures are reported through the normal path: carry them back from `loadDirectoryCmd` in `directoryLoadedMsg` and report them in `Update` via `m.reportError` (which logs each line of a joined error as its own entry and shows a toast). Careful: `applyListing` in update.go treats a non-nil `msg.err` on a listing of another path as "the directory failed to load" and keeps the pane where it was, so partial per-entry failures must not use that same field. Use a separate field (e.g. `entryErr`) or otherwise keep the listing applied while still reporting. Remove the `log` import from fs.go if it becomes unused.

Also consider `getMountedDrives` in fs.go, which returns nil without any report when `/proc/mounts` cannot be read. Either report that too or leave a short comment explaining why it's acceptable.

Add a regression test (fs_test.go or update_test.go, using `t.TempDir()`). Simulating an `Info()` failure is hard with a real filesystem, so consider making the stat step swappable the way `rename` is in fs.go. Then update DOCUMENTATION.md: remove the "Known limitations" bullet saying such entries are left out without an error. Run `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint run` and `go test ./...` before finishing.","title":"Report per-entry stat failures in directory listings","tldr":"While closing Phase 0, a review found that a directory listing silently drops any entry it can't stat and only writes a log line to stderr, which corrupts the full-screen UI. The new session would carry those errors to the error log and toast instead, with a test."}
